# FAQ-028 Engineering FAQ #28

Revision: Rev A

Q: What lubricant should be used for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 and why?
A: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-723 for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01). Background: this lubricant grade was selected for compatibility with the gearbox seals and bearing materials specified for the Heat Treat line. Rationale: the OEM compatibility testing and internal validation showed that CFW-LUB-723 provides the required film strength and corrosion protection under the process conditions encountered at the Heat Treat station. Practical example: when a mill feed change requires a full gearbox oil displacement, specify CFW-LUB-723 on the requisition and on the maintenance work order to avoid cross-contamination. Records to keep: include the lubricant part number CFW-LUB-723 on the lubrication log entry for EQ-P2-L4-RR01, attach the material receipt document, and record the batch/lot ID of the lubricant used in the equipment maintenance entry per MM-P2-L3-RR01 and SOP-P2-L3-05.

Q: What lubricant should be used for the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 and why?
A: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-101 for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03). Background: this formulation is optimized for the operational loads and environmental exposure typical at the Ring Rolling work cell. Rationale: selection focused on lubricity for sliding contacts and compatibility with existing filtration systems. Practical example: when changing over between production runs, verify the storage label and deliver CFW-LUB-101 to the point-of-use for EQ-P2-L2-RR03 to maintain consistent lubrication properties throughout the run. Records to keep: document the use of CFW-LUB-101 in the machine’s lubrication ledger and link the entry to the relevant SOP and permit references, including MM-P2-L3-RR01 and SOP-P3-L1-02, for traceability.

Q: What lubricant should be used for the Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 and why?
A: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-225 for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01). Background: this lubricant was chosen to balance anti-wear performance with chip wash-off properties specific to the Machining environment. Rationale: the formulation CFW-LUB-225 reduces built-up edge and improves surface finish consistency on parts coming directly from the ring rolling process. Practical example: before a planned machining campaign, confirm CFW-LUB-225 is staged at the tool crib and update the job traveler to reference CFW-LUB-225 for EQ-P2-L3-RR01. Records to keep: maintain purchase receipts, batch identification, and a service record documenting each replenishment and any deviation, cross-referenced to SOP-P2-L3-05.

Q: What is the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 and why must it be applied?
A: Apply mandrel clamp bolt torque of 635 N·m to Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01). Background: the mandrel clamp secures the mandrel under heavy radial loads; correct bolt preload prevents fretting and maintains concentricity. Rationale: achieving the specified preload with 635 N·m reduces cyclic loosening and extends component life while maintaining process accuracy. Practical example: during mandrel installation, use a calibrated torque wrench set to 635 N·m and follow the bolt tightening sequence specified in the applicable assembly procedure. Records to keep: log the actual torque readings, the tool calibration certificate, the operator name, and the maintenance job number in the equipment maintenance record, and reference MM-P2-L3-RR01 for historical torque application data.

Q: What is the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 and how should it be controlled?
A: Apply main ram bolt torque of 1425 N·m for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01). Background: the main ram bolts locate and retain the ram under forging loads; correct torque is critical to prevent bolt yielding and to preserve alignment. Rationale: setting the bolts to 1425 N·m achieves required clamp load while minimizing the risk of joint relaxation during heavy cycles. Practical example: when performing a ram rebuild, use a calibrated torque-control procedure to sequentially apply 1425 N·m to each main ram bolt and verify readings with a secondary inspection gauge. Records to keep: capture the applied torque values, calibration certificates for torque tools, the rebuild work order, and photographic evidence of bolt condition in the equipment history, and file these entries in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-02 and MM-P2-L3-RR01.

Related documents:
- MM-P2-L3-RR01
- SOP-P2-L3-05
- SOP-P3-L1-02

Notes on documentation practice: always record the exact part numbers and torque values as shown in this FAQ when filling maintenance records. Where procedures call for verification, reference the related document ids above to ensure consistency with controlled procedures.
